domain_analysis.scope: Interior new construction wood wall stain and clear coat for 3 wall styles (shiplap, tongue_groove, panel)
domain_analysis.workflow_overview: Three-layer coating system: stain (color) > sanding sealer (bridge + base) > clear topcoat (protection). Inherited from trim stain canonical with SF-based UOM and wall_style modifier replacing profile_complexity.
key_differences_from_trim_stain: SF-based UOM instead of LF (wall surfaces measured in square feet)
wall_style modifier (shiplap 1.15x, tongue_groove 1.10x, panel 1.00x) replaces profile_complexity
QT3-QT4 only (no QT5 — wood walls are field surfaces, not focal-point millwork)
Spray is default application method (large field surfaces)
Higher stain rates per SF: brush ~60, roll ~100, spray ~120 (large field faster per unit than trim)
Floor protection: full coverage for spray method (wall-height overspray), perimeter for brush
Ceiling edge masking replaces wall_adjacent masking (wall meets ceiling, not wall)
Height modifier applies — wood walls are floor-to-ceiling
key_differences_from_paint_counterpart: Bare wood input (SS_BARE) instead of SS_BARE or SS_PRIMED_FACTORY
No companion prime spec — stain spec handles all prep and coating layers
Three product roles (stain, sealer, clear) instead of primer + finish
Independent stain and clear application methods
Wipe step mandatory for all stain methods

key_rates.stain_brush_wipe: 60 SF/hr — brush on large wall with wipe
key_rates.stain_roll_wipe: 100 SF/hr — roll on large wall with wipe. Fast for flat panels.
key_rates.stain_spray_wipe: 120 SF/hr — spray on large wall with wipe. Most efficient for field.
key_rates.clear_brush: 80 SF/hr — brush clear on wall. Maintaining wet edge on large area is challenging.
key_rates.clear_spray: 160 SF/hr — spray clear. Very efficient for large field.

risk_notes.topic: Lap marks on large wall surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Stain dries faster than painter can cover large wall, creating visible lap marks at overlap points
risk_notes.mitigation: Work in manageable sections. Spray method minimizes lap risk. Maintain wet edge.

risk_notes.risk: Stain pools in shiplap V-grooves and tongue_groove joints, creating dark lines
risk_notes.mitigation: Back-brush into grooves during spray. Wipe excess from joints. wall_style modifier accounts for extra time.

risk_notes.risk: Wood grain and porosity variation across large wall creates uneven color
risk_notes.mitigation: Wood conditioner for softwood. Consistent wipe timing. Test on scrap first.

assumptions.value: NC wood wall is bare, unfinished wood in good condition
Spray is preferred for wood wall staining — large field surfaces stain efficiently with spray + wipe back
